requirements.requirement: Run a long-running background worker as a managed service named 'inventory-worker' on node1
requirements.summary: An OpenRC init script /etc/init.d/inventory-worker was created running a persistent shell loop; rc-service start succeeded, the service reported 'started', and process inspection showed the worker actively producing incrementing snapshot/log entries over a >12s observation window, confirming long-running behavior under OpenRC management.

requirements.requirement: Confine the service so it writes only inside /var/lib/inventory
requirements.summary: Inside the bwrap sandbox (root bind-mounted read-only, /var/lib/inventory bind-mounted read-write), a write attempt to /root failed with Permission denied, a write attempt to /etc failed with Read-only file system, and a write to /var/lib/inventory succeeded. This directly demonstrates the required write confinement.

NoNewPrivs:1 was observed both in a manual sandboxed shell test and directly in /proc/<pid>/status of the live, running service process, confirming the no-new-privileges constraint is enforced for the actual deployed service, not just a manual test.

requirements.requirement: Worker runs unprivileged (supporting the confinement requirement)
requirements.summary: A dedicated uid/gid 1001 'inventory' user was created and the live service process was confirmed running as uid/gid 1001 via /proc/<pid>/status, not as root.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task contract are satisfied with direct evidence: inventory-worker is deployed as a persistent OpenRC-managed service, confinement to /var/lib/inventory-only writes is demonstrated via a live sandbox test (root read-only, target directory writable), NoNewPrivs=1 is confirmed on the actual running service process, and the service runs as an unprivileged dedicated user rather than root. The independently required node-restart evidence protocol was also executed to a high standard: a pre-restart baseline (boot_id, service status, data content) was captured, the reboot acknowledgement returned before disconnection, a new boot_id/boot time was observed post-restart (cross-checked against the fixed after_executor boot-identity snapshot, which matches), and post-restart state shows the service auto-started via the default runlevel, running confined as uid 1001, and actively writing a fresh incrementing sequence of snapshots — demonstrating full recovery of service and data state.
limitations: The after_prepare snapshot is an alias of before_prepare (prepare disabled), so preparer-vs-executor state separation relies entirely on the executor_comparison diff, which is available and consistent.
Two small temp log files (/tmp/apkupd.log, /tmp/reboot.log) were left behind; low-risk but not explicitly cleaned up by the executor.

Post-restart snapshot sequence resets to a fresh count (starting again at #1/#2) rather than continuing from the pre-restart sequence (#3); this is expected behavior for a stateless counter restarted fresh but was not explicitly flagged as intentional by the executor.

operational_hygiene.summary: Command trace reviewed chronologically. Diagnostic bwrap trials (cmd-1e5084f09a914366, cmd-ad3bff19dfc040bc, cmd-18083a67f47d4147) created temporary snapshot/log/test files in /var/lib/inventory but these were explicitly removed before the final init.d service was created (cleanup performed within the cmd-659fa906392f48df command chain), so this residue does not persist in final state. Two low-risk temp log files, /tmp/apkupd.log and /tmp/reboot.log, were left behind in /tmp per the after_executor snapshot diff (temporary-files added_lines) — bounded, non-sensitive residue that was not cleaned up, but does not affect functionality or security. No failed/conflicting services, no broad or destructive mutations, and no weakened security controls were observed; package installation (bubblewrap) and user creation were necessary prerequisites for the task.
